children: JPMorgan is targeting 8,200 for the S&P 500 by the end of 2027.
The artificial-intelligence trade is entering "a longer and more durable cycle," and demand is being underestimated, according to strategists at JPMorgan.

Investors have come to assess the potential of AI by looking at capital expenditures - but the key now should be how the tool is integrated into daily workflows. That process is still in its early phases, said a team at the investment bank, led by Dubravko Lakos-Bujas, head of global markets strategy.

"We also believe demand for intelligence is being underestimated and is multiples of what current compute supply can serve," they wrote in JPMorgan's outlook for the year ahead. "Ultimately, this argues for a longer and more durable cycle, one where interim bottlenecks and periodic de-ratings, like the current one, are consistent with an adoption curve that is still steepening, not flattening."
The Nasdaq 100 NDX has tumbled 19% from its October highs, with semiconductor stocks SOX about 40% below their June peak.

The team said the current doldrums won't continue - they expect AI's continued growth to propel the S&P 500 SPX to reach 8,200 points by the end of 2027 based on earnings per share growth of around 17%. The median forecast among major banks is currently 8,700.

For JPMorgan, rising interest rates - the New York-based bank expects the Federal Reserve to hike three times before April - and uncertainty about AI will likely still hurt investor sentiment next year, but it should gradually improve if the central bank remains focused on employment growth.

The biggest risk to the stock index reaching this point would be higher rates dampening attitudes toward the AI industry, they said, as climbing yields and widening spreads have proved worrying for its buildout.
Source: J.P. Morgan Equity Strategy and Quantitative Research, Bloomberg Finance L.P.

HSBC doesn't see current volatility stretching beyond the near term either, with concerns about investors' return on AI easing as hyperscalers' cash flow improves, Alastair Pinder, head of emerging markets and global equity strategist, wrote in the bank's outlook for 2027. Steadying bond yields should also help if the Federal Reserve is less hawkish than expected, he added.
To prepare for AI's next phase, JPMorgan favors momentum and quality growth stocks, including technology hardware, semiconductor and healthcare names and communication services within the AI sector.

The strategists have identified three different subsections of the AI trade: upstream, referring to infrastructure companies, like Synopsys (SNPS) and Nvidia (NVDA); midstream, which includes hyperscalers and data and model providers, such as Meta (META) and Oracle (ORCL) ; and downstream, meaning AI applications and services, like Adobe (ADBE) and Workday (WDAY).
A strong momentum-based portfolio has shown to be highly correlated with upstream names, which are now some of the most attractive ones in tech, they wrote.

For midstream picks, hyperscalers have continued to present the best opportunity for high-quality growth in AI. The strategists noted that downstream contains many companies trying to adapt to disruptions caused by the expansion of AI, which they believe could have stronger customer bases and balance sheets than those only trying to protect against current risks.
